names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 22 martie, «Sfânta Muceniță Drosida, fiica împăratului Traian».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 22 Μαρτίου, «Αγία Δροσίδα και των συν αυτη πέντε Παρθένων», with the rank word and the companions left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 22 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Света Дросида.“, with Света left off, which is not a rank. The heading carries nothing else — her father's name is the body's first clause and not part of her name — so the bare forename is what the source gives; no other folder in the corpus holds a Serbian Дросида.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page 2459, «Дросида Римская, мц.», with the rank abbreviation left off. The day’s line declines the forename and names her by her father instead of by the city, «Дросиды , дщери царя Траяна», so the by-name is read off the name page.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 22 марта ст. ст. — «Мц. Дросиды , дщери царя Траяна, и с нею дев Аглаиды , Аполлинарии , Дарии , Мамфусы , Таисии (ок. 104-117).»

attestations.note: The line enumerates her five companions by name and each of them now has a folder, written in batch ru-03-22-1 off their own name pages 13979 to 13983; this folder had no `related` row at all before and gains the five. Name page 2459 gives this one day and carries the one life, life690, which is where everything the calendar says of the five is said. «Мц.» is the rank word and `martyr` was already the folder’s type; `types` and `dates` are untouched, and the line’s «ок. 104-117» sits inside the folder’s floruit of 98–117. The stored form is the name page’s own nominative with the by-name it gives her, «Дросида Римская», which the day’s line does not print. The day page carries no hymn under her name. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 22 martie — «Sfânta Muceniță Drosida, fiica împăratului Traian»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 22ης Μαρτίου — «Αγία Δροσίδα και των συν αυτη πέντε Παρθένων»

attestations.note: «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Μαρτίου εκάστου έτους.» The Greek line keeps five virgins with her — «και των συν αυτη πέντε Παρθένων» — and the page calls them the five κανονικαί and names none of them, so they are part of her entry here and not folders of their own. The page also gives her a different end from the one a reader might expect of a martyr: she escaped the palace and fell asleep in peace eight days later while praying, which is what its couplet on her says too.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 04.04.2026 (22. март ст. ст.) — „Света Дросида.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep in this folder, and the same woman: the daughter of the emperor Trajan, taken while gathering by night the bodies of those who had suffered for Christ. The entry gives no year at all, so the reign this folder already holds as a `floruit` is untouched. The five women taken with her take no row: the Prologue names none of them, exactly as the Greek line already in this folder names none — «και των συν αυτη πέντε Παρθένων» — and it says only that they were severely tortured and thrown at the last into molten copper. The Prologue adds what neither other page did: that Drosis was kept under strict imperial guard, escaped from the palace, baptised herself in a river, and gave up her soul to God eight days later. The stored form is the bare forename, because Света is not a rank and the heading carries no title at all; the daughter of Trajan is the body's first clause and not part of the name. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Η Αγία Δροσίδα, ήταν κόρη του αυτοκράτορα Τραϊανού (98-117), ο οποίος βασάνιζε και θανάτωνε πολλούς χριστιανούς» — the reign is the interval the page prints, and it gives no year for her own death. doxologia.ro gave no year at all.
